standard_prerequisites.name: Fiberwise transformation and its total map
standard_prerequisites.statement: A fiberwise transformation f : prd x:A, P(x) -> Q(x) induces a total map on the sigma types.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the map whose fiber is computed.

standard_prerequisites.name: Associativity of sigma types
standard_prerequisites.statement: Sigma types reassociate up to equivalence.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the first rewriting step at source line 750 and is used again at line 759.

standard_prerequisites.name: Paths in a sigma type
standard_prerequisites.statement: (a,u) = (x,v) unfolds into a path a = x together with a transported equality.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the step at source line 752.

core_obligations: Unfold the fiber of the total map at the point (x,v) as a sigma type of w together with a pair equality (source lines 745-748).
Reassociate the sigma types to expose a, u and the pair equality (source line 749-750).
Apply the characterisation of paths in sigma types to replace the pair equality by a path p : a = x together with trans p (f(a,u)) = v (source lines 751-752).

Reorder the components and then use the contractibility of the based path space, the omission of contractible components and associativity to eliminate a and p, leaving Sigma u:P(x), f(x,u) = v (source lines 753-759).
Recognise that last type as the fiber of the component f(x) at v, which is the statement (source lines 755-757).

proof_roadmap.step: Unfold and reassociate the total-space fiber.
Apply the sigma-path characterisation and reorder the components.
Contract the path component and read off the component fiber.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Theorem 4.7.6 at source lines 736-742: for a fiberwise transformation f and points x : A, v : Q(x), the fiber of the total map at (x,v) is equivalent to the fiber of the component f(x) at v. The author's proof (source lines 743-760) is a five-step chain of equivalences rather than a citation: it unfolds the total-space fiber and reassociates the sigma types (lines 745-750), applies the characterisation of paths in sigma types to turn a pair equality into a path in A together with a transported equality (lines 751-752), reorders the components (lines 753-754) and then eliminates the contractible path component using the based path space, the omission of contractible components and associativity (lines 755-759). The statement contains only the resulting equivalence of fibers; the intermediate type and the input of each step are invisible.
